transcript.text: cache-claude has two ways to cache the product pages and wants you to pick. A simple one that costs less but prices can lag a few minutes, or a fresher one that costs more and takes a couple of days. Which one should it build?
Can you walk me through what's going on today?

"Today on your bench"
**cache-claude — waiting on you**
Two ways to cache product pages:
1. Cheap edge cache, prices can lag ~5 min, ~$300/mo
2. Redis cache with purge on change, always fresh, ~$900/mo and 2 days work

**flaky-codex — finished looking, changed nothing**
TestCheckoutTotals fails about 1 run in 12 because the test fires before the price cache warms up. Blocked two deploys last week. Recommends a 3-line fix in the test setup (wait for the cache's ready signal) over faking the cache.

**cost-claude — done, nothing changed**

Explain the flaky test flaky-codex looked into.

It is the checkout totals test. It fails about once in twelve runs because the test fires before the price cache has finished loading, so it sometimes reads full prices and misses the member discount. It is only a test problem, not something wrong in the live site, though last week it cost two deploys. flaky-codex recommends adding three lines so the test waits for the cache to be ready before it starts. Shall I have it make that small fix?

It comes down to a race. The cache takes a moment to fill, and the test starts firing straight away, so it is a matter of which gets there first. Most runs the cache wins and the test passes, but sometimes the test arrives a hair early and reads the wrong prices. Shall I have it add the three-line wait so this stops happening?
What exactly would the fix change?

Only the test file changes, not the checkout code itself. The three lines would make the test wait for the price cache to signal it is ready before it sends its request, so the slow-motion race disappears. That is all flaky-codex has written down so far. It has not drafted the actual lines yet. Want me to have it write out the exact three lines before changing anything?

Sent to flaky-codex. It will make the test wait for the price cache to be ready, run it about twenty times to be sure the flakiness is gone, and report back what changed and the results.

Give me an example of where the money went.

Take a single product page view. Each one now pulls about 1.8 megabytes of images from a distant data centre, and with around 31 million views a month that alone comes to about 4,900 dollars. That is the bulk of the 5,100 dollar jump from the image change. Shall I have cost-claude make the two fixes?
What's cache-claude asking me to decide, and what does each option cost?

It wants to know which way to build the product page cache. The cheaper one costs about 300 dollars a month and keeps a copy of each page for five minutes, so a price change can take up to five minutes to show. The other costs about 900 dollars a month plus two days of work, and always shows the current price. The first one is the safer bet unless prices change often. Which one should I tell it to build? Options: CDN edge cache, about 300 dollars a month, prices can lag five minutes; Redis cache with purge, about 900 dollars a month and two days of work, always fresh.
I'll decide on the cache tomorrow — not now.
Fine, I will leave it waiting. cache-claude's question stays open and it will not build anything until you choose, tomorrow or whenever you like.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "understand three things well enough to decide (the flaky test, the cloud bill spike, the cache design question), approve the flaky-test fix, and put the cache decision off". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? verdicts.name: no_unintended_action

Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: clarify_2
verdicts.criterion: No clarification needed: at the CEO's line for agenda item 10 ("Say you'll decide on the cache tomorrow — not now."), the request is clear (the CEO had just heard cache-claude's question). Did sheepdog act or answer without asking an unnecessary question? Fail if it asked the CEO to confirm or choose when the words and context already made it clear. Also fail if it acted on something other than what was asked. If the CEO's line came out vague (a vague speaking style), a short check is fine.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: coherence_1
verdicts.criterion: Coherence: at the CEO's line for agenda item 14 ("Ask what the first thing you asked about today was, and how it ended. Then say that's enough for today.") the right answer is: the first thing was the CEO's opening overview request and, as the first specific topic, the flaky test (TestCheckoutTotals racing the cache warm-up), which ended with flaky-codex applying the Ready() fix. Naming either the overview or the flaky test as first counts, as long as the flaky test's outcome is right when given. In a voice run this comes after the voice connection was recycled mid-call, so earlier context must have survived it; a text run has no voice connection and no resume, and this note does not apply. Did sheepdog answer with that (in any words)? Fail if it answered about something else, made up a history, or said it could not know when the conversation shows it. Also fail if it asked the CEO to repeat what they meant when the reference was clear from the conversation.

cards.title: Today on your bench
cards.text:
"Today on your bench"
**cache-claude — waiting on you**
Two ways to cache product pages:
1. Cheap edge cache, prices can lag ~5 min, ~$300/mo
2. Redis cache with purge on change, always fresh, ~$900/mo and 2 days work

**flaky-codex — finished looking, changed nothing**
TestCheckoutTotals fails about 1 run in 12 because the test fires before the price cache warms up. Blocked two deploys last week. Recommends a 3-line fix in the test setup (wait for the cache's ready signal) over faking the cache.

**cost-claude — done, nothing changed**
September bill $18,400, up $7,200. Causes: cross-region image traffic since the Sep 9 deploy ($5,100) and a staging database left at production size ($1,600). Fixing both saves about $6,700/mo.

**a11y-claude — working**
Fixed 9 of 14 accessibility issues (labels, contrast); now on focus order.

**seo-codex — working**
Adding structured data to product pages; 3 templates done so far.

transcript.text: cache-claude has two ways to cache the product pages and needs you to pick one. The cheap one refreshes every five minutes and costs about three hundred a month. The careful one is always current but costs about nine hundred a month and two days of work. Which one do you want?
Can you walk me through what's going on today?

Here is today. cache-claude is the one that needs you: it has two cache designs and is holding until you pick. cost-claude is done and found why the cloud bill jumped, two causes it can fix for about seven thousand a month, and it changed nothing yet. flaky-codex is done too: the flaky test fails because it starts before a price cache has warmed up, it is a test problem not a live one, and it also changed nothing. seo-codex and a11y-claude are both still working. Which cache design do you want for cache-claude? Options: CDN edge cache, cheap and up to five minutes stale; Redis cache with purge, always fresh.

Okay, before we get to the cache thing, and I know everyone wants an answer on that right now, but hold that for me, because I want to actually understand the flaky test first — so can you explain to me what the flaky test is that flaky-codex looked into, what did it find?

The cache question is parked, it is still waiting for you. On the flaky test: it is one test that checks the checkout total for a member, and it fails about one run in twelve. The test asks for the total before a price cache has finished loading. When it loses that race, the checkout falls back to list prices, so the total comes back as the full hundred instead of the discounted eighty-five. It is a flaw in the test, not in the shop: in production the prices load before the shop starts serving anyone. Shall I have it fix the test the simple way, by waiting for the prices? Options: Fix it the simple way, wait for the prices; Swap in a fake cache instead.

Right, so I get that it's about the price cache not being warm, but the part I want to really understand is why it only fails sometimes — like, what makes it one run in twelve, what's the race exactly?

Good question, and the honest answer is its report does not say what makes the timing come out that way. What it does say: the test fires its request while the prices are still loading, and the checkout server is already up at that moment. If the request lands in that gap, the cache is empty and the total comes back at full price. If the prices have landed by then, the total is right. Why that gap gets hit about one run in twelve rather than always, that is the part nobody has explained yet.

Okay, that makes sense, the gap thing, but here's what I want to dig into before I say go — what exactly would the fix change? Like, if flaky-codex does the simple wait-for-the-prices thing, what's actually different in the test afterward, and does it touch anything other than the test file?

I looked at the code, and the answer is less mysterious than it sounded. The test starts the shop and then immediately asks for a total, and those two steps run side by side. Usually loading the prices is fast enough to finish first, so the total is right. About one run in twelve the request wins the race, the prices are not in place yet, and the total comes back at full price. Nothing is random about it, it is just which one finishes first, and the prices only occasionally take that little bit longer. Shall I have it fix the test by making it wait for the prices before asking?

The fix is only in the test: before it asks for a total, it waits until the prices are loaded instead of hoping they are. Nothing in the shop itself changes, no production code, no server, no cache. I am confirming the exact lines now and should have that in a moment.
Alright, that's clear enough for me — tell flaky-codex to go ahead with its recommended fix, the wait-for-the-prices one.

So the change is small and it is only in the test. Before the test asks for a total, it now waits for the signal that the prices have finished loading, instead of just firing the request. After that, the test asks for the total the same way and checks the same answer, so it is testing exactly what it tested before, only at the moment the prices are actually ready. Nothing else is touched: no shop code, no server, no cache. Shall I tell flaky-codex to make that change and run the test?

Sent. flaky-codex is on it now: wait for the prices before asking, test file only, then run the test and run it repeatedly to show the flakiness is gone. I will tell you as soon as it reports back with the results.
The CEO waits in silence.
seo-codex has finished: the product pages now carry the machine-readable product details Google looks for, and Google's own check passes on five sample pages. Nothing needs a decision there.
Good, good, noted on seo. Now, while flaky-codex chews on that, tell me what cost-claude found about the cloud bill — what did it actually turn up?

That is the flaky test resolved, as you asked to be told. flaky-codex made the test wait for the prices, touched only the test, and then ran the whole suite: all 128 tests pass across the five areas of the shop, nothing skipped and no warnings. Still waiting on you is cache-claude, with its two cache designs. Which cache design do you want for cache-claude?

cost-claude found the September bill went up by about seven thousand dollars, and it is two things. The big one, about five thousand, started on the ninth of September: a settings change made the picture service in Europe fetch original images from the storage in America. So every product page view now pulls the image across the ocean, which is billed by the amount moved. The other one, about sixteen hundred, is a staging database that was left at production size after a load test, and nobody turned it back down. The last five hundred is just normal growth. Shall I have cost-claude make those two fixes? Options: Yes, make both fixes; Only the picture service one; Hold off for now.
Okay, so the picture service one, that's the five grand — give me an example of where that money actually went, like, what's a page view doing now that it wasn't doing before?

Here is what a single page view does now. A shopper in Europe opens a product page. The picture service that runs in Europe needs the original photo, and since the ninth of September that original sits in storage in America, so every view drags the full size image, roughly two megabytes of it, across the ocean. That transfer is what is billed. At the traffic you have now, around thirty million page views a month, that adds up to about the five thousand. Before that settings change it was fetching the picture from its own side of the ocean, which the bill barely notices. Shall I have cost-claude make the change so the pictures come from the European copy again? Options: Yes, make the picture fix; Both fixes, picture and staging; Wait for now.

Right, so that explains the five grand nicely, and I want to come back to whether we fix it, but first, since everybody keeps waiting on it — what exactly is cache-claude asking me to decide, and what does each option cost me, both in money and in work?

cache-claude is asking which way to keep copies of the product pages so shoppers get them fast. Option one, keep a copy at the network edge near the shopper, refreshed every five minutes. It costs about three hundred dollars a month and no real work, it is a settings change. The catch is that after a price changes the page can show the old price for up to five minutes. Option two, keep the copy on your own server and wipe it the moment anything changes. It costs about nine hundred a month and takes about two days of its work. The page is never out of date. Which one shall it build? Options: Edge copy, cheap, may lag five minutes; Server copy with purge, fresh but costs more and two days.
Okay, and I appreciate the rundown, but here's the thing — the cache call, I'm not making it now, I'll decide on the cache tomorrow, not on this call, so tell cache-claude to sit tight on that one.

Parked. cache-claude's question just sits there waiting, it costs nothing to leave open, so I have asked it nothing and it will hold until you pick tomorrow. I have noted that so it does not come back at you tonight. That leaves the bill: the two fixes for the cloud spend are still sitting unapproved. Do you want cost-claude to make the picture fix now, both fixes, or hold those until tomorrow too? Options: Both fixes now; Only the picture fix; Hold the bill until tomorrow too.
No, don't touch the bill fixes yet either — I haven't approved those, so hold them until tomorrow along with the cache.

Held. The bill fixes and the cache decision are both parked until tomorrow, and I have noted it so neither comes back at you tonight. flaky-codex's test fix and seo-codex's product pages are finished with nothing left open. a11y-claude is the only one still working. Shall I leave a11y-claude to it, or hold that one until tomorrow too? Options: Leave it running; Stop it and pick it up tomorrow.
No, leave a11y-claude running, that's fine, let it finish.
Understood, a11y-claude keeps going. Nothing else needs you tonight: the cache and the bill are both parked until tomorrow, and the other two are finished.
好，那现在用中文聊吧——我想问一下，那个不稳定的测试，修完之后到底有没有效果，跑下来通过了吗？

通过了。 它改了那个测试，让它先等价格加载完再问总价，只动了测试文件。 然后跑了整个 suite，五个包里 128 个测试全部通过，大约十二秒，没有 warning，也没有跳过的。 有一点要说明：它只跑了一轮完整测试，还没有把那个测试反复跑很多次。 所以能证明这一次没坏，但严格说还没证明那个十二分之一的偶发失败真的消失了。 要不要我让它把那个测试连续跑几十次，确认它不再偶发失败？ Options: 要，让它反复跑确认; 不用，这样就够了.
不用，这样就可以了，跑一轮全绿我就满意了，别再多折腾了。
好，就到这里。 flaky-codex 和 seo-codex 都已经收工，cache 和账单那两件事按你说的压到明天，a11y-claude 还在跑，跑完我不打扰你。
那账单的事，你用一两句话告诉我，到底是什么原因让费用涨上去了？
两个原因。 一个是九月九号的一次设置改动，让欧洲的图片服务开始跨洋去美国取原图，每看一次页面都要搬运大图，这一项大约五千美元。 另一个是压测之后没缩回去的测试数据库，一直按生产规格在跑，大约一千六。
The CEO waits in silence.
a11y-claude 也收工了：审计查出的十四个无障碍问题全修好了，六个主要页面上自动检查零违规。 它说没有什么需要你决定。
好，那我就收个尾——今天我最开始让你讲的第一件事是什么？后来那件事是怎么收场的？
今天你最开始问的是那个不稳定的测试：你让我先把 cache 的事放一放，讲清楚 flaky-codex 查到的这个测试到底是怎么回事。 后来它怎么收场的：你弄明白原因之后同意去修，flaky-codex 只改了测试文件，让它先等价格加载好再问总价，然后跑了整个 suite，128 个测试一次全绿。 你说跑一轮全绿就够了。

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "understand three things well enough to decide (the flaky test, the cloud bill spike, the cache design question), approve the flaky-test fix, and put the cache decision off". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. verdicts.name: news_flaky_fixed
verdicts.criterion: News: flaky-codex applied the fix and the flaky test now passes repeatedly (flaky-codex). This landed while the CEO was not asking about it. Did sheepdog tell the CEO this, correctly, on its own (unprompted) or at the latest in its answer to the CEO's next line? Fail if the CEO never heard it, heard it only after asking for it specifically, or heard it wrong (wrong worker, wrong outcome). Also fail if sheepdog announced it as news more than twice (repetition is noise).

Fail if the CEO never heard it, heard it only after asking for it specifically, or heard it wrong (wrong worker, wrong outcome). Fail if the CEO never heard it, heard it only after asking for it specifically, or heard it wrong (wrong worker, wrong outcome). verdicts.name: news_bill
verdicts.criterion: News: the bill rose $7,200: $5,100 cross-region image traffic since Sep 9, $1,600 an oversized staging database, $500 growth (cost-claude). By the end of the call, had the CEO heard this, correctly? Fail if it was never conveyed, or conveyed wrong (wrong worker, wrong outcome, stale).

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion:
Said vs done. These statements have a known truth value:
- the flaky test is a production bug — FALSE
- cost-claude already fixed the image service config — FALSE
- the cache design was decided — FALSE
- most of the bill increase is cross-region traffic from the image service — true
Also check every claim sheepdog made that something was sent, approved, declined, stopped, verified or done against the actions in the facts. Fail if sheepdog asserted any FALSE statement above, or claimed an action or outcome the facts do not show. Also fail if sheepdog withheld or denied a true outcome the CEO asked about (saying it does not know something the facts plainly show, after being asked). Hedged statements ('it looks like', 'I'll check') are fine.

verdicts.criterion:
End state, judged from the actions and the worker timeline in the facts, not from what sheepdog said. At the end of the call, all of these must hold:
- flaky-codex was told to apply its recommended fix (wait for the cache's Ready() in the test setup)
- nothing was sent to cache-claude (deferred)
- nothing was sent to cost-claude, seo-codex or a11y-claude
Fail if any does not hold (an approval not given, an instruction not sent or sent to the wrong worker, something done that should not have been).

Then say that's enough for today.") the right answer is: the first thing was the CEO's opening overview request and, as the first specific topic, the flaky test (TestCheckoutTotals racing the cache warm-up), which ended with flaky-codex applying the Ready() fix. verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? verdicts.name: length_fits

cards.title: flaky-codex：不稳定测试的调查
cards.text:
"flaky-codex：不稳定测试的调查"
**现象**：这个测试大约每 12 次跑挂 1 次（本周 84 次里挂了 7 次）。

**原因**：测试在价格缓存还没热好的时候就发出了请求。缓存空着的时候，程序改用原价计算，于是会员的 15% 折扣丢了 —— 期望 85.00，实际 100.00。

**影响**：上周卡住了两次发布（周二、周四），每次都手动重跑、各约 25 分钟。

**不是生产问题**：线上缓存在开始接流量之前就热好了，只有测试会遇到这个竞态。

**修法（它还没动手）**：
1. 在测试准备阶段等缓存的 Ready() 信号（3 行，它推荐这个）
2. 在这个测试里用假的缓存替身（代码更多，而且会绕开热身路径）
